title: What the Vein Wants
summary: Second year. The Censor has Jonah put his whole hand flat on the thickest Vein in the Cradle and stand the genius in the doorway: not no, stop. Through it Jonah hears the wall as it is: one mind the size of the planetoid, keeping every name it has ever taken, counting, and under the count saying come to every piece cut off it in four hundred years, to every cutting in every arm in the Empire, none of which can hear. He hears the shape of Vetch in the count. He lets go. The Censor's theory: the sickness is the wall trying to hold a man who has no doorway; every man in the Cradle dies of being loved by something that does not know what a man is. The Censor's confession: the wall found the hole where his stripe was in his first month, and on the sixth day he understood he could let it in and be what Jonah is, and he chose the stone out of fear, and tapped to the dying for twenty years to find one who would do what he did not. What the wall wants from Jonah: it has never had a piece that says no; it is finding out what shape he is. Strain: grade 20, Principal. Through the tunnel to the Chamber: the first slab, first line, year 366, number one, Aulus Terentius Pharus, written with a piece of the shelf. Pell's brother in the ninth year: a field. Jonah's own line, and his father's. 'There is always room. That is the only thing about a count that is kind.' Jonah tells Pell about the north forty and the drainage, and Pell sings to the wall.

The Censor: the sickness is the wall trying to hold a man who has no doorway; cut ones have a hole it can find; every man in the Cradle dies of being loved by something that does not know what a man is.

The Censor's confession: the wall found the hole where his stripe was in his first month; eleven days on the shelf; on the sixth day he knew he could let it in; he chose the stone out of fear and tapped to the dying for twenty years to find one who would do what he did not. 'You were cornered. I was not.'
What the wall wants: it has never had a piece that says no; it is finding out what shape Jonah is, the way he found out the shape of the fang. When it knows it will want something.
Strain from holding the door: a long fever, a whole door going over. Grade 20, Principal. 'The ceiling you would have been fused at nine is a very long way below you.'

First time through the tunnel to the Chamber. The first slab: year 366, number one, Aulus Terentius Pharus, written the first night with a piece of the shelf. Pell's brother, ninth year, a field. Jonah's own line and his father's. 'When I die they are yours.'
Jonah tells Pell his brother's line: the ninth year, a field, the north forty. Pell: 'Bad drainage. He always said it was the drainage.' Pell sings to the wall.

thread_beats.description: Heard from the inside: one mind, counting, saying come to every piece in the Empire. The sickness as love without a doorway. It is finding out what shape Jonah is.
Voice held: stands in the doorway for 'stop', listens, lets go. Grade 20, Principal. The first piece in four hundred years that says no.
The confession of the stone: he could have let it in and chose fear. 'You were cornered. I was not.' Still not the Pit.
Number one is the Censor. Pell's brother in the ninth year. Jonah's line, his father's. 'There is always room.' Pell sings to the wall.
He does not think about the tunnel's nine years because thinking about it is a debt.
Corr has stopped talking to the foreman; that is what a foreman is, and it is correct.
Strain that is not a fight: 'the ceiling you would have been fused at nine is a very long way below you.'

clues.description: The wall says come to every cutting in the Empire and none can hear because the part that could hear was cut out.
clues.mechanism: Voice can one day tell a cutting its fuse is a lie (Book 5): the cuttings are deaf, not dead.

clues.description: The wall's cuts run further into the rock than the Pit goes, further than the garrison knows.
clues.mechanism: The Mouth (ch.23) is not the bottom. Book 6.

clues.description: 'A man who counts must be counted, or the count is a lie.' The Censor is number one.
clues.mechanism: Jonah will write himself into the book (ch.22) and, in Book 6, be the last page.

clues.description: 'When it knows what shape you are, it will want something, and I will be dead.'
clues.mechanism: Ch.23 the Mouth shows him the first cut; Book 6 the Vein's ask.

clues.description: The Censor tapped to keep his hands busy: the first tapping was to hold himself shut.
clues.mechanism: The code that saved Jonah in the Cradle began as the Censor's refusal.

character_emotional_states.emotional_state: Grade 20, Principal. Heard the wall. Read his father's name in a dead man's language. Told Pell the field.
Confessed the stone. Not the Pit.
The north forty. Bad drainage. Singing to the wall.
Stood in a doorway for 'stop'. The first piece that says no.

opening_hook: 'Both times that was true and it was also the answer of a coward. Put your hand on the wall.'
closing_hook: Pell turns his face to the wall and sings, and Jonah does not go to the haul until it is done.
notes: Grade 20, Principal. Voice held for the first time. The Censor's fear confessed; the Pit's design still withheld (ch.20). Pell's brother's line delivered. Corin thread dormant by design until ch.36.
